extracted.subtask_description: Principles for structuring a republican government to preserve liberty by separating powers, providing checks and balances, and protecting minority rights through institutional design and federalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental independence in appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department should have a will of its own; the members of each should have as little agency as possible in the appointment of the members of the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal construction would draw all appointments from the people through channels having no communication with one another. Some practical deviations and additional expense may be necessary. The judiciary is a notable exception because 'peculiar qualifications' and permanent tenure may make strict adherence impracticable: select the mode of choice that best secures required qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial independence (emoluments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each department should be as little dependent as possible on those of the others for the emoluments annexed to their offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the executive or judges are dependent on the legislature for their compensation, their independence in every other respect would be merely nominal. Secure independent emoluments to preserve practical independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constitutional means and personal motives to resist encroachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Give to those who administer each department the necessary constitutional means and personal motives to resist encroachments of the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision for defense must be commensurate to the danger of attack. 'Ambition must be made to counteract ambition' — connect the interest of the individual with the constitutional rights of the office so personal motives help check abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual task: enable government to control the governed and to control itself
rubrics_metrics.description: In framing government: first enable the government to control the governed; secondly oblige it to control itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependence on the people is the primary control, but experience shows auxiliary precautions (institutional checks, rival interests) are necessary to restrain government internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of the legislature into distinct branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Because legislative authority in a republic necessarily predominates, the remedy is to divide the legislature into different branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render branches different by modes of election and principles of action so they are 'as little connected with each other as the nature of their common functions and their common dependence on the society will admit.' Additional precautions may be necessary depending on relative strengths of branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrated check on legislature rather than absolute veto
rubrics_metrics.description: An absolute negative on the legislature (a full veto) may seem a natural defense for the executive but is neither altogether safe nor alone sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An absolute negative might not be exerted with requisite firmness in ordinary occasions and might be perfidiously abused on extraordinary ones. A remedy is a 'qualified connection' between the executive and the weaker branch of the stronger department so that the latter supports the constitutional rights of the former without severing its own departmental rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange offices so each checks the others and private interest guards public rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide and arrange the several offices so that each may be a check on the other, and that the private interest of every individual may be a sentinel over the public rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'inventions of prudence' apply throughout subordinate distributions of power: building institutional incentives and rivalries into office design is a central method to prevent concentration of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal (compound) structure for 'double security'
rubrics_metrics.description: In a compound republic (federal system), power surrendered by the people is first divided between two distinct governments, and then the portion allotted to each is subdivided among departments, creating a double security for the rights of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different governments (federal and state) will control each other while each is controlled internally by its departments; federalism supplements departmental checks and reduces the risk of usurpation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard minority rights by multiplicity of interests/classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide against the injustice of a majority by comprehending in society so many separate descriptions of citizens that an unjust combination of a majority of the whole will be improbable, if not impracticable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two methods exist: create an independent will (monarchy/aristocracy) or diversify society into many interests (republican approach). The Federalist favors the latter — a multiplicity of interests makes majority oppression unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity of interests and sects as security for civil and religious rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Security for civil rights depends on multiplicity of interests; security for religious rights depends on multiplicity of sects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The degree of security depends on the number of interests and sects, which in turn depends on the extent of country and number of people under government. More numerous and varied interests/sectors reduce the chance of oppressive combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale (extent of territory and population) increases republican stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided it lies within a practical sphere, the larger the society, the more capable it will be of self-government and the less likely a majority coalition will oppress minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small, narrow republics are more prone to reiterated oppressions by factious majorities (example: hypothetical separation of Rhode Island). A judicious modification and mixture of the federal principle allows the practicable sphere to be carried to a very great extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as the end of government
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is the end of government and civil society; stability and liberty depend on pursuing justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the stronger faction can readily unite and oppress the weaker, anarchy may reign as in a state of nature; government must be structured to secure justice for all classes, which is the fundamental aim guiding institutional design.
